questions.question: There are blind spots ____ the left and right side flat mirrors.

options.text: Immediately below
In the middle of
Above
To the left of

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately below
questions.explanation: There are blind spots immediately below and in front of each outside flat mirror. There is also a blind spot directly behind the rear bumper.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a bus driver should:

options.text: Place the vehicle in park.
Place the vehicle in first gear.
Place the vehicle in reverse.
Place the vehicle in third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: When stopping to pick up students, a school bus should be put in park. If the vehicle does not have a park gear, place it in neutral instead.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Parallel park.
Inspect your tires.
Monitor your gauges.
Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving test, you will be evaluated on your lane usage. Which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Stopping behind crosswalks
Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs. On roads with multiple lanes, complete turns in the proper lane. Stay in or move to the rightmost lane unless the lane is blocked.

questions.question: When alley docking, your vehicle should be parked:

options.text: With the front bumper on top of the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
At an angle within the boundaries of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
questions.explanation: To alley dock, first pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle into the alley parking area. Park the vehicle straight within the boundaries of the space.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus in response to a hazard, a driver should:

options.text: Ask the students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher about the hazard and decide how to respond.
Tell students to panic.
Have students open all the windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher about the hazard and decide how to respond.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest and easiest to supervise if they stay on the bus. If time allows, contact your dispatcher to explain the emergency before deciding to evacuate.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, you should not:

options.text: Ensure that the steering box is securely mounted.
Ensure that the steering box is free of leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, ensure the steering box is securely mounted. Check for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Look for power steering fluid leaks and damage to power steering hoses.

questions.question: While students load and unload a bus, the driver should:

options.text: Read a book.
Watch the process and keep an eye on the students.
Talk to other bus drivers.
Listen to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the process and keep an eye on the students.
questions.explanation: Watch students as they enter or exit the bus. Make sure they don't get caught in doors or handrails. Also make sure students move a safe distance away from the bus after exiting.

questions.question: The overhead inside mirror should be adjusted to see:

options.text: Outside of the driver's side of the bus.
All of the students on the bus.
Students in the first four rows of the bus.
In front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Position the top portion of the overhead inside mirror to show the top of the rear window. This position lets the driver see all students on the bus, including those sitting directly behind the driver.

questions.question: Properly adjusted outside convex mirrors should allow the driver to see:

options.text: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
Where the front of each front tire touches the ground.
The top of the bus.
The muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
questions.explanation: Adjust outside convex mirrors to see at least one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: If equipped, a header board should:

options.text: Be damaged.
Be loose.
Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that the header board is secure, has no damage, and is strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time
Two times
Three times
Four times

questions.correctAnswerText: One time
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you can exit your vehicle to check its position no more than one time.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes frequently.
Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test on an expressway, keep proper lane position and safe distance from other vehicles. Stay at the posted speed limit. Check your mirrors constantly to see all traffic around you.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while driving a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing in a placarded vehicle, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If a school bus needs to be evacuated, passengers should:

options.text: Always use the rear door.
Always use the windows.
Always use the front door.
Use the safest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest exit.
questions.explanation: During an emergency evacuation, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest and direct students to use it.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while operating a school bus, you should generally:

options.text: Stop between 15 and 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 100 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 10 feet before the nearest rail.
Continue across the tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop between 15 and 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should stop before railroad crossings to check for trains. Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail to see the tracks clearly. Look and listen for approaching trains before crossing.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: The emergency exits are hard to open.
The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
The emergency exits squeak.
The emergency exits cannot be reached from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits should open smoothly, have no damage, and close securely from the inside.

questions.question: When asked about the vehicle's oil during the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that the oil level is within a safe range.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the oil dipstick is, that the oil level is safe, and that the oil level is above the refill mark.

questions.question: A blind spot extends at least ____ behind a school bus.

options.text: 10 feet
50 feet
100 feet
1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: School buses have blind spots below the side mirrors, in front of the side mirrors, and directly behind the rear bumper. Rear blind spots typically extend 50 to 150 feet behind the bus, but can extend up to 400 feet depending on bus length.

questions.question: When inspecting engine compartment belts during the vehicle inspection test:

options.text: The belts should be checked for tightness, allowing up to three inches of play each.
You do not need to identify the water pump belt.
The air compressor belt should be removed.
You must identify any items that are not belt-driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must identify any items that are not belt-driven.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and fraying. Check that each belt is snug with no more than three-quarters of an inch of play. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them and check that they work properly, have no damage or leaks, and are mounted securely.
